item.research_question: How do laser metal deposited CoCrFeNiMo0.85 and Al0.5CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy coatings perform regarding erosion and corrosion resistance in three distinct geothermal environments, and how do manufacturing defects influence their degradation?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNiMo0.85 (Mo-HEA) and Al0.5CoCrFeNi (Al-HEA) coatings deposited on carbon steel (S235JR) and stainless steel (AISI 316L, 304L) substrates
item.processing_route: Laser metal deposition (LMD) using a Trumpf Trudisk 8002 5.3 kW disc laser system, Reis RV60-40 robot, and Oerlikon-Metco 10-C powder feeder under argon atmosphere; coating thickness 800–1000 µm; no post-deposition grinding or polishing
item.test_conditions: Three environments at Hellisheidi geothermal site: (1) Wellhead test at 194 °C and 14 bar (deaerated); (2) Aerated test at 90 °C and 1 bar (fluid mixed with atmospheric gas); (3) Erosion test at 198 °C and 15 bar (high-velocity fluid impact at 90° angle)
key_findings: Mo-HEA coatings on carbon steel exhibited manufacturing cracks up to 50–60 µm deep, while Mo-HEA on stainless steel showed no cracks.
Al-HEA coatings were prone to general and localized corrosion damage in all tests, forming oxide-rich films 20–40 µm thick in the wellhead test.
In the erosion test, Al-HEA coatings developed erosion pits deeper than 100 µm after a 90-day exposure period.
Erosion pits in Mo-HEA coatings were observed only at the location of pre-existing vertical cracks, where fluid turbulence increased damage.
Mo-HEA coatings on stainless steel substrates showed no adhesion damage or cracking in any of the three test environments.
Galvanic corrosion products (iron-based) formed at the interface of Mo-HEA coatings and carbon steel substrates after exposure and ambient drying.
The oxide layer on Mo-HEA in the aerated test was discontinuous, likely due to Cr concentration gradients and sluggish diffusion rates.
item.mechanism: Manufacturing cracks in Mo-HEA on carbon steel induce fluid turbulence that accelerates erosion; Al-HEA suffers from internal stresses and rapid oxidation kinetics of Al leading to non-passive, brittle oxide films; galvanic effects between noble Mo-HEA and carbon steel exacerbate corrosion at interfaces upon exposure to ambient air.
item.limitations: The study notes that surface roughness measurements were inconclusive due to scaling dominance, and the statistical null hypothesis method for erosion assessment failed due to high variability in coating thickness.
item.future_work: The formulation and production of the CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating need to be optimized to prevent cracking on carbon steel substrates; longer exposure periods are needed to verify if the discontinuous oxide layer on Mo-HEA becomes continuous.
quotes: Wide manufacturing cracks are concluded to enhance the fluid-induced erosion effect for the CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating in the vicinity of the cracks.
In the erosion test, >100 µm-deep erosion pits were observed after the 90-day erosion test period.

The reason for the discontinuous oxide layer on the surface is not fully understood, but one explanation is that Cr concentration gradients that are present in the bulk coating near the surface and sluggish diffusion rate of Cr from the high entropy material to the surface could result in slow oxide layer formation in some locations.
